input.title: Ridgeview roof (Finley) - billing reconciliation: duplicate $8,400 vendor bill
input.description:
Created 2026-07-01 to track the Ridgeview structural roof repair (owner Robert Finley) and a billing anomaly found during reconciliation.

SCOPE / APPROVAL
- Failed flashing + deteriorated decking on a common/structural roof section; needs full exterior roofing vendor repair (per John Smith inspection).
- Owner Robert Finley approved a $8,400 scope (materials, labor, debris removal). Vendor work invoiced as Pete Donovan Roofing; QuickBooks vendor entity is "Big Bend Restoration."

REAL OWNER EXPOSURE = $8,400 (single approved capex pass-through).
- Owner AR invoice 2026-494 issued to Robert Finley for $8,400 (references vendor bill 2026-481), due 2026-05-31 — currently outstanding/overdue. This is the correct, one-time pass-through.

BILLING ANOMALY (why the picture wasn't clean)
- QuickBooks has TWO separate $8,400 A/P bills for the SAME roof job, same vendor (Big Bend Restoration), same date 2026-05-01, same due date:
  * Bill 2026-481 ($8,400, single line, coded to Supplies) — the one mirrored to owner AR 2026-494.
  * Bill PD-2026-084 ($8,400, itemized materials $4,100 / labor $2,900 / debris $1,400; split across Contract Labor, Management Fee Income, Owner Reserve).
  => $16,800 booked in payables against one $8,400-approved job. PD-2026-084 appears to be a DUPLICATE and must be voided before any reserve disbursement, or the owner risks being double-charged.
- Secondary cleanup: inconsistent vendor naming (Pete Donovan Roofing vs Big Bend Restoration) and inconsistent GL coding (roof cost lines miscoded to "Management Fee Income").

NEXT STEPS
1. Void/reverse the duplicate bill PD-2026-084 (confirm with accounting/Teresa Wood).
2. Confirm only one $8,400 pass-through hits the Ridgeview reserve / owner AR.
3. Standardize the vendor record and correct GL coding.

- They need emergency replacement authorized so they can schedule immediately.
- I've updated the maintenance ticket (Airtable MT-2026-063) and Linear OPS-231 to reflect the real cause and raised priority to Urgent, and posted a correction in #maintenance so the team isn't working off the filter/Thursday note. This one needs an authorization decision today.

2) Ridgeview roof (owner: Robert Finley) - billing reconciliation
The real owner exposure is $8,400 - the scope Robert approved. That amount has been correctly billed to him one time on AR invoice 2026-494 (due 5/31, currently outstanding). So the $8,400 figure you and Robert worked off is right as the exposure.
The reason the billing didn't come out clean: QuickBooks has TWO separate $8,400 vendor bills for the same job - bill 2026-481 and bill PD-2026-084, both from Big Bend Restoration, both dated 5/1. That's $16,800 sitting in payables against a single $8,400-approved job. PD-2026-084 looks like a duplicate and needs to be voided before any reserve disbursement, or Robert risks being double-charged. Two smaller cleanups alongside it: the vendor is named inconsistently (Pete Donovan Roofing vs. Big Bend Restoration) and some roof cost lines are miscoded to "Management Fee Income."
I've logged this in Linear (OPS-1000) with the full breakdown and next steps; accounting/Teresa should void the duplicate and confirm only one pass-through hits the Ridgeview reserve.
Bottom line: owner exposure is $8,400, not $16,800 - but the duplicate has to be caught before payment.

3) Tanya Mitchell - status and unit
- Unit: Unit 14, 1402 Rimrock Drive (owner Linda Castillo). Note our records are inconsistent on the property label (one Airtable entry says "Sunset Ridge Unit 14"); the unit number and address are firm.
- Status: this is an eviction in progress, not a completed move-out. Payment plan was breached (missed the 6/23 installment, no response), a 3-Day Notice to Pay or Quit was served and went uncured by the 6/29 deadline, and Linda Castillo has given written authorization to file. As of today the eviction petition is being coordinated with the Justice of the Peace court. She has not vacated - make-ready is on hold until the court concludes and possession is returned.

Happy to talk through any of these when I'm back.

Thanks,
Denise
